questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was eligable for an Erasmus grant and had interesting courses as well as a nice camps/student lif

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a lot of stress about getting courses approved, and ended up having classes that were not my favorite, but the city is amazing and I meet so many sweet people

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as the exchange coordinaters at Tilburg uni are very available

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was two introduction days with the needed info as a monthly newsletter with cultural events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
There was a bit of confusen about transport of luggage, and the car that was supposed to pick us/it up didn't so we had to walk very far, but I don't think many other unies even think it is their responsability, so can't complain. 
they scared my a little away from the dutch language course by saying it was very demanding and needed lots of study hours, which i think is unfortiunate, as this seem to not be the case, and I think learning some dutch would have been good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Yes. They send me a lot of emails about the current houshing crisis which was a little stressful, but in the end, itwas very easy tofind a place, and the partnerorganisations of uni even had a surplus of spaces (spring 2025)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I recommended getting a place through uni and living in a dorm style place  as makes it very easy to get friends, is well located and comes with cleainng.
The Verbs is around 17 sharing kitchen and bath,so it is more social, better commen areas but cleaniness is lacking. Notre Dame has fewer people pr. kitchen (4-9?), very small commen areas, so can be less social and harder to host, but a lot more quite, clean and less fuss.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All faculties have different dates where the course registration starts. Be aware that it is very close to semester/block start, so it is quite difficult to coordinate with KU before leaving for exchange. It is however easy to get the wanted courses. You can sign up for more than you need and drop them during the semester or enrole in courses after startdate, if you find out you need more or another one is better, so it is very flexible

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact the exchange coordinator as well as rea the online guides on the uni webpage.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I sign up for, however many of the courses I saw before I applied were not availible to exchange students

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for the dutch course. They make it sound like it takes a lot of effort, but most poeple who attend don't spend mutch time. You can also always drop the course, and you don't have to take the exam, so it doesn't affect anything. You can also take it on top of you normal etc. Just try and drop it if you don'tlike, you can't sign up later

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I was supposed to take Ma courses, but there were no MA courses in psychology availible in the spring. I think there might be more in fall, as all there masters are one year, so they write the thesis in the spring, but I am not sure. 
I was however challanged either way, as some of the courses I took rested upon background knowledge I have not been tought.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
All most all exams are multible choice which affect the way thing are tought. It is mainly lectures, and a lot of people do not show up for classes. The lectures are trying to be more engaging than at KU, asking a lot of questions about the topic and peoples oppinions. It is often a small group of people who end up answering, but the teachers try anyway. 
All most all courses havea fail rate of 40%, which seems like a lot,but as long as you show up to class you'll be fine. Exams are usually mainly basen o slides and not litterature, so you won't have to read mutch to pass.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Criminoligy, Cognition and Personality
Neuropsychologicaly Assesment
Talent Management
Organizational Psychology
Topics in Psychology and Sociology Meassurements

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Criminoligy, Cognition and Personality
It is not availible at KU and the teacher is the sweetest. Very aware that people have other things out side of uni that is important, create a good enviroment and is generally and intertaining lecturer. Coming with a batchelor in Psychology form KU it is also quite easy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You will most likely  have to pay your rent for the entire period upfront.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Most thing are as expected, similar to DK but a bit cheaper. There is entrance to a lot of uni related activities and parties, and they (as well as everything else) gets more exspensive the later you book them as early bird tickets get sold out. 
I recommend going to the market on saturdays as fruit, vegetables and cheese are especially cheep there. A lot cheaper than in the supermarket and in DK. Wine is also surprisingly cheap to by in a regular supermarket! (I recoomend Aldi)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The sport center is really nice and good value for money! there is lots of different clases and facilities.
Coming in the spring semster there is also many cultural activities like Carneval, Kings day, jazz festival and markets. 
On top of that there are many student organisations. Most of them around hosting parties or doing sport, but also some academic. There are not many creative clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sport center is really nice and good value for money! there is lots of different clases and facilities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get the NS subscribtio Vrij Weekend and a Museum card and spend your weekend visiting other Dutch cities. Also enjoy Tilburg and go to some of all the bars or student parties (TPS is best)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As a Dane very easy. They are us but more interested in strangers

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn dutch and join a club/sports thing. Most clases come in an English track and a Dutch track, so you won't meet many Dutch students if you don't make an effort (I didn't)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, they are easy coming from Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Older people have so much fun. For all cultural activities it is the +40 who goes all out with costumes, day drinking and vibes. I would love to retire here.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sign up for Dutch
Be open to new experiences
Do top week and keep in contact with those people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are no availeble MA courses in the spring semestere

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many lovely people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was not particularly challenging, but finding out that Tilburg uni take an honor in failing people lead to a great amount of stress for a while

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
